title: Is Waiting a Form of Spiritual Warfare?
paragraphs:
Is Waiting a Form of Spiritual Warfare?
The Battle Nobody Sees, The War Most Christians Are Fighting Right Now, and Why God Often Does His Deepest Work in the Delay
Some battles leave scars everyone can see.
But some of the most brutal spiritual wars happen in complete silence.
And if we're honest, waiting can feel cruel.
You start asking questions you never thought you'd ask.
The uncomfortable truth is that many believers are not struggling because they lack faith.
They are struggling because they are exhausted from waiting.
Yet what if waiting is not merely a season?
What if waiting itself is one of the most intense forms of spiritual warfare a Christian can experience?
Not because God has abandoned you.
But because the enemy knows what waiting can do to a human heart.
The enemy understands that if he cannot destroy your faith, he will try to wear it down.
If he cannot stop God's promises, he will try to convince you they are never coming.
If he cannot steal your salvation, he will try to steal your endurance.
This is why waiting often feels like war.
Scripture repeatedly reveals that God's people rarely move from promise to fulfillment without passing through a wilderness of waiting.
Abraham received a promise but waited decades before holding Isaac.
Joseph received a dream but spent years in slavery and prison.
David was anointed king but ran for his life before wearing the crown.
The disciples were promised power but waited in Jerusalem before Pentecost.
The Son of God spent approximately thirty years in obscurity before three years of public ministry.
The Creator of the universe lived most of His earthly life in hiddenness.
Most people today would call that wasted potential.
The Bible repeatedly connects waiting with strength, not weakness.
"But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength..."
The Hebrew word translated "wait" is קָוָה (qavah).
This word carries the idea of binding together, twisting strands into a strong cord, and hopeful expectation.
Biblical waiting is not passive resignation.
It is the soul wrapping itself around God when circumstances make no sense.
It is remaining connected when every emotion screams to let go.
The warfare is not in standing still.
The warfare is remaining faithful while standing still.
Because God is often fighting a deeper battle than the one we can see.
We ask Him to remove the storm.
He teaches us how to survive one.
Many believers think spiritual warfare is primarily about confronting darkness.
But often spiritual warfare looks like refusing to quit when heaven seems silent.
It looks like choosing obedience without immediate rewards.
It looks like continuing to pray after disappointment.
It looks like worshiping through unanswered questions.
It looks like believing God's character when His plans remain hidden.
One of the most misunderstood examples of waiting is found in the life of Lazarus.
When Lazarus became sick, Jesus received word immediately.
The sisters expected Him to come at once.
But Scripture says Jesus intentionally delayed.
"So, when He heard that Lazarus was sick, He then stayed two days longer in the place where He was."
Because He was preparing a greater revelation of His glory.
Sometimes God's delay is not His denial.
The sisters thought they needed healing.
The same principle often appears in our lives.
Waiting feels like abandonment only when we cannot yet see the entire story.
This becomes even more powerful when we look at the Greek language of the New Testament.
"Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience."
The Greek word translated patience is ὑπομονή (hypomonē).
Remaining under pressure without abandoning your position.
It is the spiritual refusal to retreat.
In other words, biblical patience is warfare.
It is standing your ground when everything within you wants to run.
Some of you reading this are fighting that battle right now.
Waiting for prodigal children to return.
Waiting for a promise you thought would have happened years ago.
And secretly, you wonder if your faith is dying.
Maybe the truth is the opposite.
Maybe your faith is being strengthened.
Because genuine faith is not proven when prayers are immediately answered.
Faith is revealed when God seems silent and you keep trusting Him anyway.
That is exactly what happened at Calvary.
The disciples had left everything to follow Jesus.
They believed He was the Messiah.
For three agonizing days heaven seemed silent.
What nobody understood was that God was doing His greatest work behind the scenes.
That truth still changes everything today.
Many believers are standing in a Saturday season.
But God specializes in resurrection stories.
And maybe that is exactly what He is doing in your life right now.
The waiting is not proof that God has forgotten you.
The waiting may be proof that He is preparing something bigger than you currently understand.
The enemy wants you to interpret God's silence as rejection.
Scripture teaches us to interpret it as invitation.
An invitation to know God beyond His gifts.
Because eventually every believer reaches a moment where the question is no longer, "Can God answer my prayer?"
The deeper question becomes, "Will I still love Him if He makes me wait?"
That is where spiritual warfare reaches its deepest level.
But when a believer quietly says:
Those four words have shaken hell for generations.
When the answer has not arrived.
When I cannot see what You are doing.
Perhaps that is why Psalm 27:14 says:
"Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and He shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the LORD."
The Hebrew phrase חֲזַק וְיַאֲמֵץ לִבֶּךָ (chazaq v'ya'ametz libecha) literally carries the idea of strengthening and fortifying the heart.
Because sometimes the miracle is not what arrives at the end of the waiting.
Sometimes the miracle is who you become while waiting.
If this article found you in a season of delay, don't waste the waiting.
The testimony you will one day share is being written right now.
The ministry may be developing right now.
The wisdom may be growing right now.
The character may be forming right now.
The resurrection may be closer than it appears.
As a reminder to your own soul.
As a testimony that God is still worthy even in the waiting.
The waiting season may be the chapter you wish you could skip.
But it may also become the chapter that proves God never stopped writing your story.
